findings.reason: The options schema (create.ts:16-34) has no appleApiKeyId flag. The local `let appleApiKeyId` is never set before line 242, so a CI run with --apple-api-key-file/--apple-issuer-id calls appAppleApiKeysService.create at line 235 and then exits at line 244. The trigger is traced and the error text at line 212 says those two flags are enough.
findings.claim: Non-interactive iOS API-key destination creation always fails, after first uploading the .p8 key to the server.
findings.evidence: The options schema (lines 16-34) has appleApiKeyFile and appleIssuerId but no appleApiKeyId option. appleApiKeyId is only a local, `let appleApiKeyId: string | undefined;` (line 53), so it is always undefined. With `--apple-api-key-file X --apple-issuer-id Y` and no TTY, authMethod becomes 'apiKey' (line 193). Lines 233-240 then call `appAppleApiKeysService.create(...)`, and line 242 `if (!appleApiKeyId) { if (!isInteractive()) { consola.error('You must provide the Apple API Key ID...'); process.exit(1); } }` exits. There is no flag that can supply the value. The command's own non-interactive error message (line 212) tells users that passing --apple-api-key-file and --apple-issuer-id is enough, which it is not.

findings.reason: appGoogleServiceAccountKeysService.create (line 182) and appAppleApiKeysService.create (line 235) run before later prompts that can process.exit, and before appDestinationsService.create. Neither key service has a delete method and the key IDs are never printed.
findings.claim: Private keys are uploaded before the remaining inputs are collected and before the destination is created, so a later exit or cancel leaves them orphaned on the server.
findings.evidence: Android: `appGoogleServiceAccountKeysService.create(...)` (line 182) runs before `appDestinationsService.create(...)` (line ~318). iOS: `appAppleApiKeysService.create(...)` (line 235) runs before the Key ID, Issuer ID and Team ID prompts (lines 242-315). Each of those prompts can `process.exit(1)` or be cancelled; prompt() calls process.exit(0) on cancel. No delete call exists in either key service, and the key IDs are never printed.

members.claim: Service-account and API private keys are uploaded before the remaining inputs are collected and before the destination is created, so any later cancel, missing input or API error leaves the uploaded key on the server with no cleanup and no ID shown.

findings.reason: Lines 160-169 upload the profiles, then appCertificatesService.create runs at line 172 and updateMany at line 186. Nothing catches or cleans up on failure, and the certificateId field in CreateAppProvisioningProfileDto is never used.
findings.claim: Provisioning profiles are uploaded before the certificate is created, with no rollback when a later step fails.
findings.evidence: Lines 160-169 loop over `appProvisioningProfilesService.create(...)`. Then `appCertificatesService.create(...)` runs at line 172, then `updateMany(...)` at line 186. Nothing is rolled back if a later step throws. A wrong second --provisioning-profile path also throws from `fs.readFileSync(profilePath)` (line 161) after the first profile is uploaded. CreateAppProvisioningProfileDto already has a `certificateId` field (src/types/app-provisioning-profile.ts:16) that the service sends, which would let the profiles be uploaded after the certificate, but the field is never used.

members.claim: Provisioning profiles are uploaded before the certificate exists. A failed certificate upload (for example a wrong password) leaves the profiles orphaned, and a failed link step leaves a created certificate without its profiles, so a retry makes a duplicate.
